clue.text: (and 4) Jolly hitters with ad hoc clues for hanger-on

parts.note: the second word of the Latin phrase ad hoc, used on its own
keys are explanations or clues to a puzzle, as in an answer key
ticks are parasites that cling on, the classic hangers-on; plural to match the hitters

explanation.surface: Cheerful players with sticks are offered improvised hints about some clinging companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria's wordplay is loose: 'for' only links. 'Jolly hockey sticks' is the British catchphrase for hearty girls'-boarding-school enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockey sticks are the clubs players hit the ball with, and the phrase jolly hockey sticks is a familiar British expression of schoolgirl heartiness.

clue.text: (and 25) Pack with would-be 22s, known in heaven as…

definitions.note: with 25 across the light completes the hounds forming a pack

explanation.walkthrough: 22 is BANNER: in 2002 Parliament was debating a ban on fox hunting with hounds. The trailing dots lead into 2 down, the Latin name of the constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack is a group of hounds kept for the chase, which is what these animals are.

clue.text: (and 12) …4, possibly native to the Channel Islands

definitions.meaning: surface: sticks, perhaps, continuing the previous clue
setter's reading: Jersey is famous for walking sticks made from the stalks of its giant cabbage

explanation.surface: Sticks of some kind, perhaps from Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues 1 down: the Hunting Dogs are known in the sky as this word plus 12 across. 4 across is STICKS, and Jersey's giant cabbage stalks are traditionally made into walking sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Canes are walking sticks, and the Channel Island of Jersey is known for making them from tall cabbage stalks.

clue.text: Quiet among listeners? This could help achieve it

indicators.note: one thing among others sits between them, so the letter goes in the middle of the pair

parts.note: an ear is a listener
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
lug is slang for an ear

explanation.surface: Silence among an audience, and here's a gadget that might bring it about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listeners' is plural, giving two words for ear, one either side of P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug pushed into the ear canal blocks noise, so it helps bring quiet to the wearer.

clue.text: See 1 across
Volunteers afforded a gift of money

definitions.note: two senses: a gift, and an ancient sum of money

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
afforded or granted for a while

explanation.surface: Volunteers were given a cash present.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition covers both senses: a natural gift, and the talent of the ancient world, a large weight of silver or gold used as money.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural ability, and in antiquity it was also a weight of precious metal used as currency.

clue.text: Get money — half the treasure — and turn to drink

parts.note: coin is money in its metal form

indicators.note: half here means only half of the word treasure is kept, its first four letters

parts.note: a U-turn, so turn gives the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone grabs cash, splits the hoard, and then takes to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn to drink' reads as a phrase meaning take up drinking, but turn supplies a letter and drink alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, a drink served neat or in cocktails.

clue.text: Means of reproduction for awkward clients

indicators.note: awkward suggests something clumsy and out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fertility help offered to difficult customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' suggests breeding; here it is copying a design.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out template lets you copy the same pattern or lettering repeatedly by painting through it.

clue.text: Means me — after I intervene between enlisted man and sergeant

indicators.note: to intervene between two things is to stand in the middle, so this letter comes between the soldiers

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier
taken as written
a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer
taken as written, placed at the end

explanation.surface: A soldier explains his finances, standing between a private and a sergeant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in 'a man of means'. ME goes last because of 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Means are money or wealth, and unearned income from investments or inheritance gives someone independent wealth.

clue.text: One negative will come before long

parts.note: one, as the indefinite article
a prefix or word meaning not

explanation.surface: A single refusal will arrive soon enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned adverb for soon, shortly, in a little while.

clue.text: 18's travels — right and left in the dry — in French 27s

parts.note: first half of the French word for streets; 27 is the street entry

the second 'in' places the whole built string inside the French word for streets

parts.note: rest of the word for dry, parched
start of the word for dry, which wraps the next letter
standard abbreviation for left
standard abbreviation for right
end of the French word for streets

explanation.surface: A writer's journeys, told in fragments about directions, drought and French roads.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside ARID to make ALRID; R joins the front, and the lot sits inside RUES, French for streets. 18 is COBBETT, author of Rural Rides (1830), an account of horseback tours of England.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cobbett's best-known book recounts his journeys on horseback through the English countryside, so it is literally his travels.

clue.text: Girl I'm upsetting with religious book

indicators.note: to upset is to turn over, so the words before it are read the other way round

parts.note: a lass is a girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to distressing a young woman with a holy text.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the book containing the texts used for Mass throughout the Catholic year.

clue.text: See 2
Get garage repaired with sand and gravel

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Have a garage fixed up using builder's materials.
explanation.definitionFit: In building, aggregate is the crushed stone, gravel and sand mixed with cement to make concrete.

clue.text: Rude rebuff from 2 in the garden

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a blown rude noise of contempt

definitions.note: a fruit that grows on garden canes
definitions.meaning: second meaning: soft fruit picked from canes grown in the garden

explanation.surface: A gardener's scornful dismissal from among the canes.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is CANES; this soft fruit grows on canes. Blowing one is making a vulgar spluttering noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The red berry grows on cane plants, and the derisive noise comes from rhyming slang 'raspberry tart'.

clue.text: Perceive the charge to be a pound?

parts.note: a fee is a charge
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Sense whether the price is a single pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel is to sense or become aware of something, through touch or intuition.

clue.text: See 27
Successes prevent Kate acting

parts.note: wins are successes
an old sense of let, to hinder, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' usually means allow; the archaic sense is the opposite, surviving in tennis and in British passports.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Winslet is the English actress who starred in Titanic, so she is a Kate who acts.

clue.text: Cleans during typically straight talk

indicators.note: something happening during another sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: start of the proverbially straight object, as in 'straight as a ___'
to scour is to clean by scrubbing

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up while delivering frank, plain speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Typically straight' points to DIE, from the simile 'straight as a die'; SCOURS sits inside it. 'Straight talk' looks like one phrase, but only 'talk' is the definition.

clue.text: Writer with horse to put shirt on — and the shirt?

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
to put your shirt on something is to stake everything on it
a T-shirt

explanation.surface: A gambling writer backs a horse with everything, including his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Putting your shirt on a horse means betting all you have; the second shirt is a T-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cobbett was an English radical journalist and pamphleteer of the early nineteenth century, so a famous author.

clue.text: Trickery is no big deal, they say

parts.note: something slight is small and unimportant

explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means skilful deception or dexterity, as in sleight of hand used by conjurors.

clue.text: Spire said to have body?

parts.note: flesh is the body, as against the spirit

clue.text: Relating to a molecular process where love pierces the monster Caliban

love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

clue.text: Standard wielder of blue pencil?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flag carried on a pole
second meaning: a censor, one who bans things

explanation.surface: An ordinary editor who wields a blue pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue pencil is the censor's or editor's tool for striking things out, so the wielder is someone who bans.

clue.text: Prompt good starter to enter undressed

clue.text: The brother from Rome with fellow medallist in Devon

parts.note: Italian for the, as said in Rome
Italian title for a friar or brother
prefix meaning joint or fellow, as in co-worker
a Member of the Order of the British Empire, who wears its medal

explanation.walkthrough: 'From Rome' serves both 'The' and 'brother', calling for Italian words. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilfracombe is a seaside resort town on the north coast of the county, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: See 1 down
Gigolos when grown up sell childish things

definitions.meaning: first meaning: toy boys once they become adults

definitions.note: a clause: they sell childish things

explanation.surface: Ageing gigolos end up hawking juvenile trinkets.
explanation.walkthrough: A toy boy is a woman's much younger lover; grown up, the boy becomes a man. The other sense is people who make or sell toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Toymen are traders in children's playthings, and humorously the adult version of kept young lovers.

clue.text: (and16) Two ways of surviving in the urban jungle

definitions.text: Two ways of surviving in the urban jungle

parts.words: Two ways of surviving in the urban jungle
parts.note: the whole clue describes the quality of city-savvy people, while 'two ways' hints that the answer is built from two words each meaning a way: a road, and an old word for manner

explanation.surface: A tip on how to stay alive in a tough city.
explanation.walkthrough: STREET is a way in the sense of a road; WISE is an old word for way or manner, still alive in clockwise and otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone streetwise has the shrewdness needed to cope with the dangers of city life.
